ai_show_review.summary: High‑energy ‘82 Charlottesville show – killer China>Rider, monster High Time & stellar SBD
ai_show_review.review:
The September 14, 1982 Dead show at the University of Virginia is a pure burst of late‑summer fire. The band rides a relentless high‑octane second set that opens with a smoking China Cat Sunflower → I Know You Rider segue and rolls through Samson & Delilah, a soaring High Time, and an expansive Space → Aiko jam that blossoms into an uplifting Iko Iko. The first set isn’t far behind, delivering the unforgettable Lazy Lightning → Supplication → Deal triple‑threat and a gritty El Paso that shows the group’s willingness to swing from country‑flavored storytelling to deep improvisation. Across every recording the energy stays locked in, making this one of ’82’s most consistently tight performances.

Audio‑wise the Clugston soundboard capture (gd82-09-14.sbd.set2.clugston.7547.sbeok.shnf) is the clear winner – bright, crystal‑clear mix with punchy drums and excellent definition that lets Jerry’s sweet lead tone, Phil’s beefy bass, Brent’s solid keyboards and Bill & Mickey’s interlocking rhythms shine through. Audience tapes also hold up surprisingly well, especially the “excellent” audience recording that preserves the crowd vibe while still delivering a clear stereo image. Whether you listen to the pristine SBD or an audience version, this show rewards every Deadhead with its relentless groove and standout jams.

best_recording.reason: Excellent soundboard source with bright, clear mix and standout drum definition; captures the high‑energy second set in pristine detail.

key_highlights: Smoking China Cat Sunflower → I Know You Rider segue that fuels the whole show
Monster High Time with soaring guitar work and tight rhythm section
Epic Lazy Lightning → Supplication → Deal sequence in the first set
Space → Aiko jam leading into a jubilant Iko Iko, plus a post‑drums groove

band_performance.Jerry: High‑energy lead work throughout; sweet tone on High Time, effortless licks on China>Rider and powerful vocals that ‘sing from his instrument’.
band_performance.Phil: Audible, beefy bass that anchors the jams; highlighted moments include a smoking stage monitor at the end of Rider and strong accents on the closing Deal.
band_performance.Bob: Prominent in the Space→Aiko jam; dialed‑in organic tone on rhythm guitar and standout vocal delivery on ballads like El Paso.
band_performance.Keys: Brent Mydland delivers solid, supportive keyboards, with particularly strong playing during the China>Rider transition and steady comping throughout.
band_performance.Drums: Bright, punchy drum mix with excellent definition; Bill & Mickey lock in tight grooves that drive the high‑energy flow of both sets.
